run._args_note: ONE bound root, not a config flag plus a store flag. fleet.json is the DECLARED fleet and samples.jsonl is what we have actually read from it; splitting them across two flags lets the two disagree about which fleet you are looking at.

_no_companion_note: THE ABSENCE IS THE DECLARATION. This provider deliberately ships no companion, because sampling spends a real API call against the very budget it reports — a background poller would be an instrument that quietly consumes what it measures, and would do it on every box forever. The caller asks; nothing polls. If someone later adds a timer, it belongs here as a declared companion and it needs an argument for why the cost is worth it, not a default.
_why_this_file_exists: Same reason as the other three lifts: the run spec lived on apps/provider-manager, which made a fact about this PACKAGE the property of one CONSUMER of it. With this file the app is a client that names its backend, and the backend says how to start itself.
_verbs_note: EVERY route this server answers, not just the read ones. It declared only state and sample while serving five, so account, assign and switch were routed nowhere and 404'd -- and the surface reported nothing, because a failed write looks exactly like a write that has not been polled back yet. Every WRITE in PROVIDER MANAGER was silently dead. The asymmetry that hid it: a verb declared REQUIRED but unserved refuses to boot, loudly; a verb SERVED but undeclared fails at call time, silently.
